standard.title: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations
standard.description: plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations that include information, arguments and details that develop a theme or idea, organising ideas using precise topic-specific and technical vocabulary, pitch, tone, pace, volume, and visual and digital features
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations that include relevant information, facts, arguments and details using appropriate vocabulary, pace, volume and visual features (AC9E5LY07). They have not yet specifically developed a sustained theme or idea across a presentation, deployed pitch and tone deliberately, or used technical vocabulary for persuasive effect.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations that develop a theme or idea with information, arguments and details, using precise vocabulary, voice delivery features, and visual and digital elements.

nodes.label: Planning and organising ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a spoken or multimodal presentation that organises information, arguments and details to develop a theme or idea, selecting appropriate vocabulary and structural choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a plan for a spoken or multimodal presentation that identifies the theme or idea, organises at least three supporting points logically, and notes key vocabulary choices.
nodes.typical_width: Plan a report or argument that sequences ideas logically and provides supporting detail; select precise topic-specific and technical vocabulary for key concepts; plan how graphics, sound and visuals will enhance audience engagement and understanding.
wider: Plan an argument on a curriculum content issue, identifying claims, evidence and persuasive techniques appropriate to the audience
Plan and set goals for a presentation in a written or digital journal, and monitor progress against those goals
success_criteria: Produces a plan that identifies a theme or idea and organises at least three supporting points logically
Identifies at least two key vocabulary choices appropriate to the topic and audience

nodes.label: Voice delivery for effect
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deliberately use pitch, tone, pace and volume in spoken delivery and explain the effect on audience understanding.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate deliberate variation in at least two voice features (pitch, tone, pace, or volume) in a practice delivery; explain one effect on audience understanding.
nodes.typical_width: Experiment with pitch, tone, volume and pace effects in formal presentations; recognise and demonstrate how voice effects aid audience understanding; rehearse and reflect on voice delivery choices.
wider: Record and review own delivery, identifying where voice features supported or undermined the presentation's purpose
Compare delivery of the same content at different pace and volume settings and evaluate which best serves the audience and content

response_modes.reason: Voice delivery requires repeated rehearsal practice — students who understand voice features conceptually still need iterative practice before deliberate control is available under the pressure of live delivery.

success_criteria: Demonstrates deliberate variation in at least two voice features during a presentation
Explains the intended effect of at least one voice choice on the audience

nodes.label: Delivering a complete presentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can deliver a spoken and/or multimodal presentation that develops a theme or idea using precise vocabulary, deliberate voice features, and effective visual and digital elements.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a spoken or multimodal presentation that develops one theme or idea with at least three supporting points, uses at least one piece of precise topic vocabulary, and demonstrates at least one deliberate voice delivery choice.
nodes.typical_width: Deliver a structured spoken or multimodal presentation that develops a theme or idea through information, arguments and details; use precise technical vocabulary; apply deliberate voice delivery features; integrate visual and digital elements to enhance communication.
wider: Present an argument on a learning area content issue with claims supported by evidence, careful topic vocabulary and audience-appropriate persuasive techniques
Evaluate the presentation against stated goals (from the planning journal) and identify specific improvements for a future presentation

response_modes.reason: Delivery integrates planning (Node 1), voice control (Node 2), content knowledge, vocabulary precision, and visual integration simultaneously — the whole-presentation act is where all components must coordinate.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Evaluating a presentation against self-set goals and identifying specific improvements is rich metacognitive practice that develops habits of reflection transferable to all public communication.
success_criteria: Delivers a presentation that develops a clear theme with at least three supporting points
Demonstrates at least one deliberate voice delivery choice and uses at least one piece of precise topic vocabulary
